label: paragraph_title
text: CHING MING

label: text
text: CHINESE FESTIVAL OF "PURE BRIGHTNESS."

label: text
text: ANCESTOR WORSHIPPING

label: text
text: “Ch’ing Ming” festival (Pure Brightness) this year falls on Easter Monday, when the Chinese will worship their ancestors' tombs.

label: text
text: Europeans will have already noticed the approach of the festival by the applications from their staffs and servants for leave to return to their native villages, should such be anywhere close at hand.

label: text
text: There will be large numbers who will pay their respects to departed ancestors. Most of the Chinese cemeteries are in "the neighbourhood of Pokfulam and Aberdeen and it has been stated that extra buses will be put or to cope with the increased traffic.

label: text
text: The day will be observed as a partial holiday by Chinese: in Hongkong, without any special celebrations.

label: text
text: In most cases, the worshipping consists of the usual burnt offerings, and meditation.

label: text
text: Ching Ming, as one of the greater Chinese festivals, is the fifth of the twenty-four solar periods into which the year is divided. It is sometimes named the Festival of Tombs, for special thought is given to the dead, while graves are put in good order. It was anciently the day for the re-kindling of fires, which had been extinguished three days before. It is also a time for picnics and excursions into the country, and houses are decorated with foliage. Various things connected with this festival remind the Western student of the Christian Easter.

label: text
text: Han Shih (meaning "cold food") is a Chinese festival held immediately before Ch'ing Ming. In olden times, for three days no fires are supposed to have been kindled; hence the name of the feast.

label: text
text: The feast is said to have its origin in the death of Chieh Chih-t'ui, but this is only a more modern explanation.

label: paragraph_title

TO BE ENFORCED ON
APRIL 12.

label: text
text: PRECAUTION MEASURE.

label: text
text: The Head of the Sanitary Department notifies that dogs going abroad in the public thoroughfares or elsewhere on and after April 12, until further notice, will be required to be muzzled.

label: text
text: Any owner whose dog is found abroad unmuzzled will be liable to a fine of $100.

label: paragraph_title
text: PAPERS LONDON POLICE SEIZED.

label: text
text: "NATIVES OF ORIENT."

label: text
text: There has been considerable discussion of late (says a London paper in mail week) on the advisability of the Home Office disclosing more of the discoveries made by the police in the raid on the Communist Party headquarters last October, which resulted in the conviction and imprisonment of twelve of the Communist leaders.

label: text
text: The haul was one of the largest of the kind ever made by Scotland Yard.

label: text
text: Detective-Sergeant Renshaw, of the Special Branch, stated during the court proceedings that a quarter of a million items of documents, books, files, and the like were seized.

label: paragraph_title
text: 12 Van Loads:

label: text
text: They made 12 van loads, and their removal occupied seven hours.

label: text
text: At the trial only a few documents were rendered as evidence, and the impression was given that the Attorney-General had decided to produce the minimum number thought necessary.

label: text
text: Subsequent events, such as the implication of university undergraduates and natives of the Orient in Communist propaganda, have suggested that discoveries of a serious nature, other than those revealed in court, were made.

label: text
text: Only certain facts relating to the extent to which the British Communist Party has been subsidised from abroad since 1920 were disclosed to the jury.

label: text
text: Members of Parliament's beliefs that the publication of further details of the discoveries would be of service.

label: paragraph_title
text: ENGINEERS

label: text
text: DINNER OF VOLUNTEER COMPANY.

label: text
text: SIR C. CLEMENTI PRESENT

label: text
text: H.E. the Governor, Sir Cecil Clementi, presented musketry prizes won at last Sunday's annual shoot at a dinner on Thursday night of the Engineer Company, Hongkong Volunteer Defence Corps.

label: text
text: Major R. Melville Smith submitted the toast of the guests and spoke of the honour the Company felt at the presence of His Excellency, Hon. Colonel of the Corps. In the course of a humorous speech, the speaker referred to the references which had been made locally with regard to the application of H.M. King George's wish that British troops should be supplied with the "best" beer.

label: text
text: He didn't quite like to infer that the Engineer Company was composed of beer specialists, said the speaker, and history did not relate how far their R.E. collaborators were responsible for the shortage. But he was sure that the Company would like to turn the suggestion into an invitation, and he could assure His Excellency that he would find in the Canteen two British beers and one German. The speaker had every reason to suppose that the quality was all that it is supposed to be.

label: text
text: H.E. the Governor presented the following prizes in the course of the evening:

label: paragraph_title
text: POMPÉII FIND.

label: text
text: BRONZE STATUETTES OF STREET VENDORS.

label: text
text: Four characteristic and highly interesting statuettes have just been brought to light at Pompeii. All four represent a "Placentarius" (pastry vendor) and are executed in a most artistic manner in bronze covered with silver patina. While keeping to the character of an ambulatory vendor, the artist chose the type of a Jew, bald and bent, perhaps one of those street amblers who earned a miserable living in the markets of Pompeii and Naples by selling eatables, such as snails, honey cakes, and other popular dainties. The figures hold on high large rectangular trays. The right hand grasps the throat, and they smack their tongues with evident glee, just like the pastry cooks of our own day in Naples, who call out in dialect! Cheste a lava & luglio ca to reerea o'stomaco, to signify that no one else sells such delicious cakes.

label: paragraph_title
text: ARCTIC FILM.

label: text
text: Locked in the Ice, a British ship, carrying fifteen people, two of them women, will brave the hardships of the next Arctic winter off Devon Island, a Canadian Island north of Baffin Island, and six hundred miles south of the North Pole.

label: text
text: This expedition, organised by Mr. Victor Dines, a fur-trader. Is to make a fila based on a story specially written by Miss Winifred Graham. Short interest films of whaling, polar bears, and so on will also be taken, and the vessel, which sails under Commander F. A. Worsley, chief navigator of Shackleton's "Quest" will start for home in the summer of 1927. The entire enterprise will be British, and U.C personnel is to include four British film actors.

label: paragraph_title
text: RELIGIOUS WORK.

label: text
text: EVANGELISATION IN NEW TERRITORIES.

label: text
text: ANNUAL MEETING

label: text
text: The conditions in the New Territories, in the various Churches this year, have been very good, states the annual report of the Hongkong and New Territories Evangelisation Society.

label: text
text: The report goes on to state that the members baptised have increased and the contributions have not decreased. The preachers and members of Committee in the various places have been sincere and faithful, and have shown resource in dealing with affairs, and the evangelistic work in the villages has often far exceeded expectations.

label: text
text: The accounts showed a total income for the year of about $8,400, raised in fairly equal proportions by European and Chinese contributions.

label: text
text: The annual meeting at which the report was presented was held in the lecture hall of Union Church, the Rev. J. Kirk Maconachie presiding.

label: text
text: Addresses by the- Society's Chinese workers followed, the Rev. H. R. Wells translating.

label: text
text: The superintendent evangelist, Rev. Li Shu-kwal, who, together with Mr. Wells takes general oversight of the work, made some interesting references to the fact that in spite of all the troubles in Kwangtung and Hongkong, no difficulties had appeared in the relations between foreign and Chinese elements in the whole course of the year's operations. The reason for that, in his opinion, is that in Christian work and principle, goodwill and consequent unity are achieved, and there lies the hope of the future.

label: text
text: Amongst those present were the Revs. Dr. Pearce and J. H. Johnson, Dr. (Mrs.) Hickling, Dr. (Miss) A. Sydenham, Dr. Ashton, Dr. Early, Dr. Hollings, Capt. W. Davison, Messrs. A. S. D. Cousland, E. B. Cubey, A. H. Mackenzie, J. L. MacPherson, C. C. Hickling and many Chinese ladies and gentlemen. Mrs. Ho Shu-lau, Hon. Secretary, and Mr. E. R. Dovey, Hon. Treasurer, were also present, the latter pointing out that with more funds the work could be much extended.
